concepts.title: Ecosystem - Components and Energy Flow
concepts.definition: An ecosystem unites living organisms with the non-living parts of their surroundings - biotic components like plants, animals and decomposers with abiotic air, water and soil; energy enters through producers, flows one way along food chains and webs, and only about ten per cent passes to the next level.
concepts.key_idea: Ten per cent law: energy shrinks at every step up the food chain.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc113.txt sections on ecosystem and energy flow
question_patterns: define ecosystem and list its biotic and abiotic components
draw a food chain of four levels and label the trophic levels
why is only ten per cent of energy transferred to the next trophic level
what would happen if decomposers were removed from the ecosystem
differentiate producers, consumers and decomposers with examples
how does a food web differ from a food chain - explain

solution_steps.explain: Living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) parts together form the ecosystem.
Producers feed herbivores, which feed carnivores, losing energy at each step.
Decomposers return nutrients, completing the cycle.

concepts.title: Ozone Layer - Depletion and Protection
concepts.definition: High in the stratosphere, a layer of ozone molecules shields life by absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation; chlorofluorocarbons released from refrigerators and sprays broke this shield, and international agreements banning CFCs have since begun healing it.
concepts.key_idea: A sun-shield of ozone, thinned by CFCs, was rescued by global agreement.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc113.txt section on ozone layer depletion
question_patterns: what is the ozone layer and where is it located
how does ozone protect life on earth - explain the UV shielding
what chemicals caused ozone depletion - name and explain the mechanism
which international agreement banned ozone-harming chemicals
what effects would ozone depletion have on living beings
why is the ozone hole more severe near the poles - discuss

solution_steps.explain: Ozone absorbs dangerous ultraviolet rays of the sun.
CFCs release chlorine atoms that split ozone molecules.
Banning CFCs worldwide lets ozone slowly rebuild.

concepts.title: Managing Our Garbage - Biodegradable and Non-biodegradable Waste
concepts.definition: Wastes divide into two families: biodegradable wastes like peels and paper that decomposers break down, and non-biodegradable wastes like plastics and pesticides that persist for ages; segregation, composting, recycling and reduced use keep the environment livable.
concepts.key_idea: Segregate at source: let nature digest the biodegradable, recycle the rest, refuse the worst.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc113.txt section on managing the garbage we produce
question_patterns: differentiate biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes with examples
why is segregation of waste important - explain the methods
how is composting done - describe the process
what problems do plastic wastes cause - discuss
list the steps an individual can take to reduce waste
why do pesticides like DDT accumulate in food chains - explain biomagnification

solution_steps.explain: Separate degradable kitchen waste from plastics and metals.
Compost the degradable; recycle the reusable; bury the rest safely.
Using less and refusing disposables shrinks the garbage problem.
